text: In the photonic design hierarchy, why is each component reduced to a frequency-dependent scattering (S-parameter) matrix?
choices: Because S-parameters can describe only lossless devices
Because scattering matrices sample the optical carrier at 193 THz directly
Because the S-matrix is extracted once from a rigorous simulation, then reused as a cheap compact model when composing thousands of components in a circuit simulator
Because they remove the need for any rigorous electromagnetic simulation
explanation: Extracting S(lambda) once from a broadband FDTD run yields a reusable compact model, so thousands can be composed at negligible cost in a SPICE-like circuit simulator — the heart of compact-model thinking. Choice 0 is false (S-parameters describe lossy devices too); choice 1 is backwards (baseband envelopes avoid sampling the carrier); choice 3 inverts it — the S-matrix is derived FROM a rigorous simulation.
